missions.title: Choose the Cloud Service Boundary
missions.objective: CV0-004 1.1 - Cloud service models and shared responsibility
missions.briefing: Northstar Health is moving four distinct workloads to the cloud. Select the service model that fits each workload and the customer responsibility that remains after the provider assumes its portion of the stack.
instructions: Select one service model for each workload.
Select the customer duty that correctly applies under that service model.

tasks.label: Hosted scheduling product
tasks.prompt: Clinicians use a complete browser-based scheduling product operated by the vendor.

tasks.label: Managed application runtime
tasks.prompt: Developers deploy custom web code while the provider operates and patches the runtime and platform.

tasks.label: Legacy imaging server
tasks.prompt: The application requires administrator control of the guest operating system, middleware, and installed imaging software.

tasks.label: Event image resize
tasks.prompt: Code runs only when an image arrives and no persistent server or runtime administration is required.

customerDuty: Manage identities, access, application configuration, and customer data
Maintain application code, configuration, identities, and data
Patch and secure the guest OS, middleware, applications, and data
Maintain function code, event configuration, permissions, and data

hosted-scheduling.customerDuty: Manage identities, access, application configuration, and customer data

managed-runtime.customerDuty: Maintain application code, configuration, identities, and data

legacy-imaging.customerDuty: Patch and secure the guest OS, middleware, applications, and data

event-image-resize.customerDuty: Maintain function code, event configuration, permissions, and data

explanations.hosted-scheduling: A complete provider-operated application is SaaS. The customer still controls its users, access settings, application configuration, and data.
explanations.managed-runtime: A provider-managed application platform is PaaS. The customer remains responsible for application code, configuration, identities, and data.
explanations.legacy-imaging: Guest operating-system control identifies IaaS. The customer must secure and maintain the guest OS, middleware, applications, and data.
explanations.event-image-resize: Event-triggered code on a provider-managed runtime is FaaS. The customer owns the function code, event configuration, permissions, and data handling.

missions.tableLabel: Cloud service model and shared-responsibility decisions

missions.title: Release the Cloud Platform
missions.objective: CV0-004 2.2-2.5 - Deployment, migration, automation, and provisioning
missions.briefing: A migration program has four release lanes. For each lane, choose the deployment strategy, the automation approach demanded by the evidence, and the dominant provisioning requirement.
instructions: Use the release and rollback constraints to select the deployment strategy.
Use the explicit automation and resource clues to select the remaining fields.

tasks.label: Parallel customer portal
tasks.prompt: A complete parallel environment can be built from repeatable definitions. Traffic must switch without downtime and return immediately if validation fails.

tasks.label: Limited API exposure
tasks.prompt: A high-risk API release begins with 5% of requests. A script must use variables and conditions to increase the traffic share only after healthy measurements.

tasks.label: Batched service update
tasks.prompt: A twelve-node stateless service can replace only two nodes at a time. Desired application settings must remain versioned and identical across the fleet.

tasks.label: Single internal server
tasks.prompt: A single nonclustered internal server has an approved maintenance window, no spare capacity, and a fixed cost ceiling. The repeatable update command is stored in version control.

automation: Script with variables and conditional traffic logic

limited-api.automation: Script with variables and conditional traffic logic

explanations.parallel-portal: Blue-green uses two complete environments and supports immediate traffic reversal. IaC creates the repeatable parallel stack, and uninterrupted cutover makes availability the dominant requirement.
explanations.limited-api: A canary limits initial exposure. Variables and conditions implement the measured traffic increase, while traffic distribution makes network provisioning the binding concern.
explanations.batched-service: A rolling release replaces small batches while healthy nodes remain online. Versioned desired settings are configuration as code, and minimum healthy capacity protects availability.
explanations.single-internal-server: An in-place update changes the existing server during its maintenance window. A versioned script makes the action repeatable, and the no-spare-capacity constraint makes cost dominant.

missions.title: Observe and Scale
missions.briefing: The operations team must make three workloads observable and select a scaling approach that responds to each workload's actual demand pattern.
instructions: Select the telemetry source that best exposes the stated condition.
Pair it with an actionable alert response and the appropriate scaling approach.

tasks.label: Cross-service API latency
tasks.prompt: A customer request crosses six services. Operators must find the slow hop, alert on a p95 breach, and add stateless API instances as request load rises.

tasks.label: Unpredictable queue backlog
tasks.prompt: Workers fall behind unpredictable event bursts. Operations needs backlog evidence, an actionable age threshold, and additional workers when queued events increase.

tasks.label: Predictable month-end processing
tasks.prompt: A known month-end window needs more workers. Failed-job evidence must remain searchable and operations must be alerted when the failure rate crosses its approved limit.

telemetry: Centralized retained job and application logs
alertResponse: Alert and triage when p95 latency breaches the service threshold
Trigger the queue-response runbook when queue age exceeds the limit
Alert operations when the failed-job rate exceeds the approved threshold
Collect the signal without assigning a response

cross-service-latency.alertResponse: Alert and triage when p95 latency breaches the service threshold

queue-backlog.alertResponse: Trigger the queue-response runbook when queue age exceeds the limit

month-end-processing.telemetry: Centralized retained job and application logs
month-end-processing.alertResponse: Alert operations when the failed-job rate exceeds the approved threshold

explanations.cross-service-latency: Distributed tracing follows one request across service boundaries. A p95 alert supports triage, while load-triggered horizontal scaling adds stateless API capacity.
explanations.queue-backlog: Queue depth and age quantify the backlog. An age threshold drives an actionable response, and event-triggered horizontal scaling adds workers as events accumulate.
explanations.month-end-processing: Centralized retained logs preserve failed-job evidence. A failure-rate alert supports response, while scheduled scaling fits a known recurring processing window.

missions.title: Protect and Retire Resources
missions.objective: CV0-004 3.3-3.4 - Backup, recovery, and resource lifecycle
missions.briefing: Operations must protect three data resources, recover them in ways suited to the incident, and complete the correct update or retirement action for each resource.
instructions: Choose the backup plan that satisfies the recovery evidence.
Choose the recovery method and lifecycle action independently.

tasks.label: Transaction database
tasks.prompt: The database has a low RPO, needs targeted object restoration, and must retain persistent data while a supported minor release is applied.

tasks.label: Ransomware-affected file service
tasks.prompt: A clean recovery environment is available. The service uses a weekly baseline and daily change protection, and compromised resources must not be retired before evidence and restored data are validated.

tasks.label: Unsupported archive platform
tasks.prompt: A long-term archive is reaching end of support. The entire retained dataset may be requested and must remain recoverable after the platform is retired.

backupPlan: Weekly full plus frequent incremental backups
Weekly full plus daily differential backups
Encrypted full backup stored off site
Snapshots stored only with the source resource
recoveryMethod: Granular recovery of affected database objects
Parallel recovery into a clean isolated environment
lifecycleAction: Test and apply the supported minor update while preserving persistent data
Preserve evidence, validate restored data, then decommission compromised resources
Verify retention and restore capability, then retire the unsupported resource
Delete the resource before testing recovery

transaction-database.backupPlan: Weekly full plus frequent incremental backups
transaction-database.recoveryMethod: Granular recovery of affected database objects
transaction-database.lifecycleAction: Test and apply the supported minor update while preserving persistent data

ransomware-file-service.backupPlan: Weekly full plus daily differential backups
ransomware-file-service.recoveryMethod: Parallel recovery into a clean isolated environment
ransomware-file-service.lifecycleAction: Preserve evidence, validate restored data, then decommission compromised resources

unsupported-archive.backupPlan: Encrypted full backup stored off site
unsupported-archive.lifecycleAction: Verify retention and restore capability, then retire the unsupported resource

explanations.transaction-database: Frequent incrementals support the low RPO, granular recovery targets only the affected objects, and a tested minor update preserves supported persistent service safely.
explanations.ransomware-file-service: Differentials contain changes since the weekly full. Parallel recovery avoids overwriting evidence, and decommissioning follows preservation and restored-data validation.
explanations.unsupported-archive: An encrypted off-site full backup protects the complete retained set. Bulk recovery validates whole-dataset recoverability before the unsupported platform is retired.

missions.title: Secure Cloud Administration
missions.objective: CV0-004 4.3-4.4 - Identity, access, and security best practices
missions.briefing: Security must approve access for administrators, a deployment workload, and contractors. Configure the access method, authorization model, and primary hardening control for each identity.
instructions: Select the secure access method that fits the identity and interface.
Apply the narrowest authorization model and the best-practice hardening control.

tasks.label: Linux administrators
tasks.prompt: Federated administrators with MFA must manage private Linux hosts through one monitored management entry point.

tasks.label: CI/CD deployment workload
tasks.prompt: A nonhuman pipeline calls deployment APIs and must not store a long-lived human credential or expose secrets in its repository.

tasks.label: Project contractors
tasks.prompt: External contractors authenticate through their home directory and may use the web portal only for resources assigned to one project group.

accessMethod: Federated MFA through a bastion host using SSH
Short-lived workload identity token through approved programmatic access
SAML federation with MFA to the web portal
hardening: CIS-hardened bastion with least-privilege administrative permissions
Approved secrets manager with enforced API security
Zero Trust conditional access with least privilege
Permanent credentials stored in source control

linux-administrators.accessMethod: Federated MFA through a bastion host using SSH
linux-administrators.hardening: CIS-hardened bastion with least-privilege administrative permissions

deployment-workload.accessMethod: Short-lived workload identity token through approved programmatic access
deployment-workload.hardening: Approved secrets manager with enforced API security

project-contractors.accessMethod: SAML federation with MFA to the web portal
project-contractors.hardening: Zero Trust conditional access with least privilege

explanations.linux-administrators: Federated MFA through a bastion gives administrators a controlled SSH path. RBAC and a CIS-hardened least-privilege bastion reduce management-plane exposure.
explanations.deployment-workload: A short-lived workload identity supports programmatic access without human credentials. A least-privilege role, secrets manager, and API security protect the automation path.
explanations.project-contractors: SAML federation with MFA avoids unmanaged local identities. Group-based authorization and Zero Trust conditional access restrict contractors to approved project resources.

missions.title: Defend and Detect
missions.objective: CV0-004 4.5-4.6 - Cloud security controls and suspicious activity
missions.briefing: The security operations team has four evidence packages. Identify the suspicious activity and select the cloud control that most directly addresses the demonstrated attack path.
instructions: Classify the activity from the evidence rather than from a single keyword.
Choose the most directly applicable control for the demonstrated path.

tasks.label: Encoded injection attempts
tasks.prompt: A public application receives encoded injection payloads in request paths and parameters before the requests reach the application service.

tasks.label: Distributed traffic flood
tasks.prompt: Thousands of unrelated source addresses exhaust a public endpoint with a large traffic flood while the application remains otherwise healthy.

tasks.label: Unauthorized mining process
tasks.prompt: A new process consumes nearly all compute on a workload and contacts a known mining pool even though no mining software is approved.

tasks.label: Phished identity token
tasks.prompt: A fake identity-provider message is followed by token use from an unusual location against resources the user does not normally access.

control: Restrictive IAM policy with approved authentication conditions

phished-token.control: Restrictive IAM policy with approved authentication conditions

explanations.encoded-injection: Encoded malicious request data indicates vulnerability exploitation. A WAF inspects application-layer requests and can block the payload before it reaches the application.
explanations.distributed-flood: Many sources exhausting a public endpoint indicate DDoS. DDoS protection is designed to absorb or filter distributed traffic attacks.
explanations.unauthorized-miner: Unapproved mining activity and extreme compute use indicate cryptojacking. Endpoint protection can detect, isolate, and remove the workload process.
explanations.phished-token: The fake identity message is phishing. Restrictive IAM policy and approved authentication conditions reduce what a stolen token can access.

missions.title: Troubleshoot the Cloud Citadel
missions.objective: CV0-004 6.1-6.3 - Deployment, network, and security troubleshooting
missions.briefing: Nine incident cards contain deployment, network, and security evidence. Match each incident to the corrective action that directly addresses the demonstrated cause.
instructions: Use the evidence in each card to identify the actual fault domain.

tasks.prompt: An IaC deployment calls an API version the provider has retired. The current supported API succeeds in a manual test.
The required accelerator instance family is unavailable in the selected region, while the same request succeeds in an approved alternate region.
Autoscaling stops exactly at the account's documented resource maximum even though application health and regional capacity remain normal.
Authentication failures correlate with several hosts drifting seven minutes from the trusted time source after a network-policy change.
Two newly connected cloud networks use overlapping address ranges and cannot route reliably despite permissive security rules.
A migrated VM works within one host but fails across hosts because its destination port group applies the wrong VLAN tag.
A partner integration fails immediately after the approved TLS policy removes a deprecated cipher suite offered by the old client.
An unapproved remote-management agent appears on a production workload and creates an unexpected outbound connection.
A deployment identity can pass any role and was used from an unusual address to attach administrator permissions.

options.label: Update the component definition to a supported API version and validate the migration
Select a supported region or an approved compatible resource design
Request an approved quota increase or redesign to remain within the quota
Restore NTP reachability and configuration, then verify time synchronization
Renumber one network or redesign the address plan to remove overlap
Correct the virtual-switch VLAN tag and verify the trunk path
Update the partner client to a supported cipher suite and validate negotiation
Isolate the workload, preserve evidence, remove the software, and investigate installation
Remove the wildcard privilege, contain the identity, and review the audit trail

explanations.retired-api: The provider retired the API version, so the component definition must migrate to a supported interface and be validated before deployment.
explanations.regional-accelerator: The evidence isolates regional service availability. A supported region or compatible approved design resolves the unavailable resource dependency.
explanations.account-quota: Stopping at the documented account maximum identifies a service quota. An approved increase or a lower-quota design addresses the actual limit.
explanations.time-drift: The policy change interrupted trusted time synchronization. Restoring NTP and verifying clock alignment addresses the authentication failures.
explanations.overlapping-networks: Overlapping address ranges prevent reliable routing even when security rules allow traffic. The address plan must be corrected.
explanations.incorrect-vlan: The wrong virtual-switch tag places cross-host traffic in the wrong VLAN. Correcting the tag and validating the trunk restores the intended segment.
explanations.deprecated-cipher: The client offers a cipher the approved policy no longer accepts. Updating the client and validating negotiation resolves the deprecation issue.
explanations.unapproved-agent: The unauthorized software and outbound connection require containment, evidence preservation, removal, and investigation before restoration.
explanations.wildcard-role: Wildcard role-passing enabled privilege escalation. Removing the permission, containing the identity, and reviewing audit evidence addresses both access and impact.
